results.identification: A secondary, bullet‑point synopsis of the UK Conservative Party’s 1997 general election manifesto (“You can only be sure with the Conservatives”), compiled from the manifesto’s themes and pledges. It is not the official text but a later summary produced by an unnamed summarizer (likely user- or AI-generated) drawing on the 1997 Conservative manifesto.
results.evidence: The heading says “Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary.” Content matches distinctive 1997 UK Conservative policies: opposing the EU Social Chapter and a national minimum wage; ‘keep options open’ on the single currency with a referendum and “unlikely by 1999”; proposals to privatise London Underground and National Air Traffic Services; complete rail privatisation; support for grammar schools and Assisted Places; ‘Basic Pension Plus’-style funded pensions via NI rebates for new entrants; responses to BSE; opposition to devolution to Scottish/Welsh assemblies; CAP reform; CCTV expansion and mandatory minimum sentences. These are all hallmarks of the 1997 UK Conservative general election manifesto under John Major.

results.identification: A summary of the UK Labour Party’s 1997 general election manifesto, ‘New Labour: Because Britain Deserves Better,’ including its five-pledge card; published by the Labour Party (April 1997, United Kingdom).
results.evidence: The text lists Labour’s 1997 ‘five pledges’ (class sizes, halve time to sentence persistent young offenders, cut NHS waiting lists via £100m from bureaucracy, a windfall levy to get 250,000 under‑25s into work, and no rise in basic/top income tax with VAT on fuel cut to 5%); promises Bank of England reform; creation of a Scottish Parliament, Welsh Assembly, and a London mayor; a national minimum wage set by an independent Low Pay Commission; ending hereditary peers’ voting rights; a free vote on a complete ban on handguns; establishment of a Food Standards Agency, NESTA, the University for Industry and Individual Learning Accounts; a Freedom of Information Act; and the stance of ‘no case for new nuclear power stations’ alongside a referendum on joining the single currency.

results.identification: A bullet-point summary of the UK Conservative Party’s 1997 general election manifesto (John Major era), i.e., the Conservative Party (UK) 1997 manifesto.
results.evidence:
References that are distinctly Conservative (UK, 1997):
- Education: "expand Assisted Places," "allow some selection and facilitate creation of grammar schools" (Labour opposed these in 1997; Conservatives supported them).
- Europe: "oppose adding EU-level social and employment regulations… protect existing opt-outs" (the Tory Social Chapter opt-out stance); "keep options open on a single currency; no entry without a national referendum."
- Privatisation: "complete rail privatisation; privatise London Underground… privatise National Air Traffic Services" (core Conservative policy in 1997).
- Housing: "continue Right to Buy" (signature Conservative policy).
- Taxes/spend: aim for "20p basic income tax rate" and top rate "no higher than 40p," spending below 40% of GDP (classic Conservative positioning).
- Citizen’s Charter/Chartermark (a John Major Conservative initiative).

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 1997 general election manifesto (“Make the Difference”), i.e., the Lib Dems’ manifesto for the 1997 UK general election.
results.evidence: “Invest £2bn per year (funded by +1p on basic income tax).” (the Lib Dems’ signature 1997 ‘1p on income tax for education’ pledge); “Proportional representation for all elections; fixed four‑year terms” (core Lib Dem constitutional reform platform); “Local Income Tax” (long‑standing Lib Dem policy); “Support entry to a single European currency if criteria met and backed by referendum” (Lib Dem pro‑EU stance with a referendum); “Royal Commission on drugs” (distinctive Lib Dem justice policy); “Repeal Section 28… equal age of consent… end discrimination in the armed forces” (Lib Dem LGBT equality agenda); “No subsidies for nuclear; no replacements at end of life” (Lib Dem 1997 anti‑new‑nuclear line); “Restore free eye and dental checks” (Lib Dem NHS pledge); “0.7% ODA/GNP within 10 years” (Lib Dem development target); “Retain Trident with reduced warheads” (Lib Dem defence position in 1997).

results.identification: The Referendum Party’s 1996–97 Draft Referendum Bill/pamphlet (issued by Sir James Goldsmith’s Referendum Party) proposing a national referendum on the UK’s relationship with the European Union.
results.evidence: References to offering a referendum choice between being "part of a federal Europe" or "an association of sovereign nations within a common trading market"; proposing the vote "before or alongside the next general election"; arguing recent European treaties transferred powers and required public consent; and criticizing other parties for limiting any referendum to the "single currency" rather than the broader constitutional question.

results.identification: A summary of the Scottish National Party’s 1997 UK general election manifesto (the SNP’s independence-in-Europe program), published by the SNP.
results.evidence: References specific to Scotland and the SNP’s 1990s platform: independence route via a majority of Scottish MPs then a referendum; creation of Scottish Defence Forces, removal of nuclear weapons and phased NATO withdrawal; abolishing Skye Bridge tolls; ending nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; prioritizing Rosyth refits; asserting North Sea jurisdiction; support for Gaelic and Scots; land reform to abolish feudal tenure; explicit 1997 dating.
